title: SHERLOC: Structured Diagnostic Localization for Code Repair Agents
abstract: LLM agents solve repository-level coding tasks through multi-turn tool use, but utilize half their budget on locating faults before editing. Dedicated localization frameworks have emerged, yet are still evaluated as file retrieval rather than actionable diagnosis, producing locations without the diagnostic context a repair agent needs. We introduce SHERLOC (Structured Hypothesis-driven Exploration and Reasoning for Localization), a training-free framework pairing a reasoning LLM with compact repository tools and self-recovery, without fine-tuning or multi-agent orchestration. SHERLOC reaches state-of-the-art localization across model scales: 84.33% accuracy@1 on SWE-Bench Lite and 81.27% recall@1 on SWE-Bench Verified; at ~30B parameters, it matches or outperforms other agentic methods. Injecting our locations and diagnostic findings into repair agents yields, on average, +5.95 pp resolve rate on SWE-Bench Verified while cutting localization and total tokens by 36.7% and 23.1%.

significance.justification: The paper demonstrates a 5.95 percentage point improvement in resolve rate on SWE-Bench Verified while reducing token usage by 23.1%, directly impacting how builders should approach code repair agent architecture.

novelty.justification: SHERLOC introduces a structured hypothesis-driven approach that pairs reasoning LLMs with compact repository tools and self-recovery, representing a substantial new variation from prior localization frameworks.

reproducibility.justification: The paper describes a training-free framework with clear methodology, though it doesn't explicitly mention code or artifacts being publicly available, suggesting minor reproduction friction.

clarity.justification: The paper is well-written with specific performance metrics (84.33% accuracy@1, 81.27% recall@1) and clearly scoped claims about token reduction and performance improvements.

topical_fit.justification: This paper directly addresses LLM agent performance for code repair tasks, sitting squarely in the applied-AI sweet spot for builders working with LLMs on coding problems.
